SMTO-AUT-0003 — The admin password was for a different account than the Gateway's

GUID: 56919f95-bb6f-4a82-8fe5-5b1d72c4da8a
Slug: credential-scope-mismatch
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: aut

What happened

  • SMTO was given an administrator username that doesn't match the account the Gateway uses on that computer, so it didn't send the password or run the command.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check which computer the Task used by looking at the Gateway picker next to Add context in the message box. Each Gateway, the helper program that runs commands, uses one account, and the password must belong to that account.
  2. If that's the wrong computer, select the right Gateway in that picker before sending your next message. Choosing the Gateway first makes sure the password only goes to the computer you intended.
  3. If it's the right computer, ask the person who manages it which account the Gateway or its SSH login uses, and give SMTO that account's password when asked. Administrator rights are checked for the Gateway's own account, so a password for any other account can't be used.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and its step is marked Elevated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send another person's password to this computer, and don't paste any password into the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Managed elevation rejected the request before using the credential because the supplied sudo username differs from the selected Gateway's local account or the verified SSH destination user.

What this means

  • Managed local or SSH elevation compares the supplied username with the selected execution account and rejects a mismatch before credential use. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Managed local or SSH elevation compares the supplied username with the selected execution account and rejects a mismatch before credential use.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the intended account with the verified Gateway or SSH target user, without exposing the password.

How to fix it

  • Compare the supplied sudo username with the Gateway process account (pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid())) for local elevation, or with the verified SSH known-host user for remote elevation (ssh_privilege._plan). Supply the password for that exact account through the private ask_user/sudo_password flow, or select the correct Gateway or SSH target before starting a new operation.
  • Use the intended selected account through the secure credential form, or explicitly select the correct Gateway/account before a new operation. Do not send another account’s password to this target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The credential account matches the verified selected execution account.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
